entry.title: Trump says U.S. won't attack Iran before midterms. And, ICE agent shoots man in NYC
entry.summary: Trump announced that the U.S. will not attack Iran ahead of the midterms. And, a 28-year-old man is receiving treatment at the hospital after an ICE agent shot him in the neck.

entry.title: Why American investors love European defense startups
entry.summary: As European defense spending takes off, just about half of the funding in Europe's defense tech industry is coming from American investors this year. One reason why: European investment firms have restrictions on how they can invest.

entry.title: Why we remember: One student's journey into memory
entry.summary: Why one teen can't let go of the time he ate fries with his great-grandpa.

entry.title: Republican congressman tries to outrun a potential blue wave in New York toss-up seat
entry.summary: Rep. Mike Lawler, R-NY, is in a tight race for re-election in a toss-up district that could help determine control of Congress in November.

entry.title: Fill in the blank in the quiz: A plague research employee in Russia died from ____
entry.summary: Plus: Nobels! Protests! Ambiguous quotes! A mysterious death in Russia!

entry.title: ChatGPT for Teens has special safeguards. A watchdog group finds most don't work
entry.summary: A study from Common Sense Media says most safeguards in ChatGPT for Teens failed. The chatbot talks to teens like a friend and doesn't alert parents when users talk about self-harm and suicide.

entry.title: Why mailing a ballot close to Election Day may get it rejected for a late postmark
entry.summary: If you're using the U.S. Postal Service to return a ballot close to Election Day, officials recommend getting it postmarked at a post office to avoid getting caught up in mail processing changes.

entry.title: A student hated reading for years. Her podcast explores finding the right diagnosis
entry.summary: Middle schooler Cora Walsh of Long Island, N.Y., has won the 2026 NPR Student Podcast Challenge with a story about her journey with dyslexia.

entry.title: In Central African Republic, deported immigrants find themselves in limbo
entry.summary: The Trump administration says it has deported more than 25,000 people to countries to which they have no ties. NPR spoke to three men who say it feels like they've lost control over their own lives.
